title: Marguerite and the Ember
premise: Edmund Reyes, a temple scribe indentured by debt, has survived fifteen years in the city of Vhalen by selling harmless charms while magic itself is outlawed. When tonight's date surfaces in a century-old book of prophecies, he and Marguerite—a dragon-blooded woman hiding her inheritance—are pulled into a prophecy that names one of them as the ember-bearer who will either reignite the ancient war or let the last dragon-fire die forever. Hunted by the Inquisitor General and betrayed by the temple that owns Edmund's debt, they flee toward the Ashvault where the final flame sleeps. In the end, Edmund pays his debt in the only currency left: he takes the fire into himself, burning away his memories of Marguerite so she can carry the ember into hiding—until she returns years later to give him back one memory at a time.
about_author: A. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about what people owe, what they remember, and what they choose to forget.

chapters.title: The Date That Was Written
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Copying ledgers in the temple archive, Edmund finds tomorrow's date inked in a sealed prophecy book alongside a sketch of his own face. He tells himself it's coincidence until the page begins to glow. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine—the first crack in fifteen careful years.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite buys a luck charm from Edmund's market stall, hiding the heat that rises in her palms when the temple guards pass. She notices the scribe's shaking hands and the prophecy-light leaking from his satchel. Emotional beat: two people recognizing fellow survivors without knowing why.

chapters.title: What the Ember Remembers
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The prophecy book drags Edmund through a vision of the Dragon War's end: a city burned, an oath sworn, and a woman with Marguerite's eyes sealing the last flame. He wakes in the market square with Marguerite kneeling over him—and her blood glowing gold. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The temple calls in Edmund's debt early, offering freedom if he surrenders the prophecy book and names the 'anomaly' he was seen with. He lies for the first time in fifteen years. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of choosing a stranger over safety.

chapters.title: Ash Under Her Skin
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite confesses her inheritance: her grandmother was a dragon's oath-keeper, and the ember's call has been waking in her since childhood. She never asked for it; she only wanted to be ordinary. Emotional beat: relief and shame tangled together in finally being seen.

chapters.title: Inquisitor General Corvane
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The Inquisitor General reads the same prophecy and understands its true stakes: whoever holds the ember holds the empire's founding legitimacy. He orders the market quarter sealed. Emotional beat: cold, patient menace—a man who believes cruelty is simply thoroughness.

chapters.title: The Rooftops of Vhalen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Edmund and Marguerite escape the sealed quarter across the rooftops, guided by Marguerite's instinct for heat and Edmund's knowledge of the temple's patrol charts. A guard dies when Marguerite's fear flares. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into guilt—her power costs lives.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Confession
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Cornered in a cellar, Edmund admits his charms were never magic—they were placebos, kindness sold as protection. Marguerite laughs until she cries: the fraud kept hope alive better than real spells ever did. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared smallness.

chapters.title: The Oath-Keeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They find Sera, the last living oath-keeper, dying in the flooded cisterns. Sera explains the choice: the ember must be carried by a willing vessel or it will burn its way into an unwilling one. Emotional beat: grief and urgency—an inheritance arriving too late to refuse gracefully.

chapters.title: What Corvane Wants
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Interrogating the captured temple abbot, Corvane reveals his motive: his family died in a magical plague the dragons failed to prevent, and he wants the ember extinguished forever—not hoarded. Emotional beat: the villain made legible, almost sympathetic.

chapters.title: The Road Through Cinderfen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The journey to the Ashvault crosses the Cinderfen, where war-dead still smolder after a century. Marguerite hears the dead dragons speaking; Edmund maps their route from fragments of prophecy verse. Emotional beat: the past made physical, unavoidable terrain.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The temple sells their location to Corvane; Edmund's old mentor leads the ambush. Edmund bargains with his own capture to buy Marguerite time, and learns his debt was never money—it was always meant to end this way. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that raised him.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Corvane doesn't torture Edmund; he shows him records proving Marguerite's line caused the plague Edmund's own family died of. The lie is half-true, which makes it work. Emotional beat: doubt planted like a splinter, working deeper with every mile.

chapters.title: The Vault Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Alone, Marguerite reaches the Ashvault and finds the door answers only to an oath spoken in dragon-tongue—which she never learned. The dead dragons offer to teach her, at the price of her human memories. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: A Memory, Traded
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite trades her memory of her mother for the first word of the oath, then realizes the pattern: the whole oath will cost her everything human. She begins anyway. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, which is the only kind that counts.

chapters.title: Rescue and Reckoning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Edmund escapes, confronts Marguerite at the vault, and demands the truth about the plague. She gives him Sera's letters proving Corvane falsified them—but Edmund can no longer fully trust his own mind, poisoned by the interrogation. Emotional beat: love tested against manufactured doubt.

chapters.title: The Last Word of the Oath
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Understanding dawns: the prophecy says the vessel must be willing and unclaimed—unowned. Edmund burns his debt-contract in the vault's threshold flame, freeing himself, and speaks the final word with Marguerite. Emotional beat: liberation and horror in the same breath.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Gates
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane arrives with the imperial legion and offers Marguerite a bargain: surrender the ember and live. When she refuses, he gives the order to breach the vault, knowing it may kill everyone inside—including the legitimacy of the throne he serves. Emotional beat: conviction pushed past reason.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The vault breaches; the ember flares wild and begins consuming Marguerite from within. The only way to steady it is a second vessel to share the load—one who owes nothing and chooses everything. Edmund steps into the fire. Emotional beat: climax—two people holding a sun between them.

chapters.title: What Edmund Paid
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. To contain the ember, Edmund feeds it his memories of Marguerite—every charm, every rooftop, every confession. He survives, hollowed, remembering duty but not her. Corvane, seeing the fire mastered rather than weaponized, stands down and lets them go. Emotional beat: devastating cost, quietly rendered.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Months later, magic is decriminalized and Marguerite runs a modest school for oath-keepers. Edmund works in the rebuilt archive, polite to a woman he doesn't recognize. She visits daily, telling him one true story each time. Emotional beat: grief braided with stubborn hope.

chapters.title: One Memory at a Time
chapters.summary: Shared POV. On the anniversary of the vault, Marguerite gives Edmund a charm—his own design, a placebo—and tells him the story of the rooftops. Something in him warms; the ember, it turns out, keeps what it's given. He says her name like a word remembered mid-sentence. Emotional beat: resolution—not restoration, but the beginning of return.
